body:
The commitment field you show is a well-formed position, but it is not self-sufficient for the task as posed. It names a reformulation (sequencing rather than correct reading), a settled item (quiet-week convergence), a best-specified move (the avoidant-friend conversation), an observation about the requester's load position, a set of non-commitments, and a list of open problems. What it does not expose is the body that supplies the readings, the probe, the backward record, the separability test, the recorder-disclosure condition, or the grounds for treating a quiet week as convergent. I can still work on some of what follows from taking these commitments up, but I have to mark where I am filling in from the commitment field's own wording rather than from material I can see.

Taking the sequencing reformulation up: if the real unsolved problem is what to do this week given no probe and no record, then the first commitment it generates is to identify at least one action available this week that is not itself one of the contested moves. The requester has three people, changing schedules, an avoidance pattern, and a history of agreements whose meanings diverged. The commitment field already concedes that if no such action exists, the reformulation collapses into a restatement of the deadlock. I do not have a case that distinguishes the two, and neither, apparently, does the author. So the honest use of this reformulation is as a search instruction: look for a this-week action in the gap between 'agree who does what' and 'disagree what the agreement meant.' If the search returns nothing, the reformulation is not doing work and should be dropped.

Taking the quiet-week convergence up as settled: I can only carry it as a claim about what the chain has established, not as a fact about the flat. A quiet week might be informative in ways the chain has not considered. For instance, if quiet weeks cluster around one person's changed schedule, they may be evidence about that schedule rather than about the prior agreement. If quiet weeks are simply weeks when the avoidant friend is absent, they may be evidence about avoidance rather than about convergence. I do not have a showing either way, and the commitment field does not supply one. So I would carry it, but with a note that its evidential value depends on a contrast class the chain has not specified.

Taking the avoidant-friend approach up: the specified move is to ask for their view of the group conversations, not why they avoid. That is a clean specification because it does not presume the avoidance is the problem. The attached cost is that if it produces more avoidance, that counts against the approach. I would add that one flat is a small case, so a single engagement is weak evidence for the approach and a single further avoidance is weak evidence against it. Neither outcome settles the framing. The move is still the best-specified thing in the commitment field, and I would try it before trying any private record, though the commitment field explicitly does not commit to that order.

Taking the observation about the requester's load position up: the claim is that the requester's position in the load distribution affects what the requester can propose, not just what should be disclosed before a record. That is plausible in ordinary household terms. If the requester is currently carrying most of the load, a proposal to formalize the existing distribution will read as self-serving; if the requester is carrying least, a proposal to redistribute will read as an accusation. The commitment field says it has no evidence either way. I do not either. What I can say is that this observation is a reason to identify the requester's position before choosing a proposal, and that identifying it is itself a move that may need to be done privately or with care, since 'I think I do most of the work' is one of the contested moves in disguise.

On the non-commitments: I note them without treating them as a ranking. The commitment field does not rank the three readings, does not order the private record against the avoidant-friend conversation, does not specify who the requester is in the flat, does not claim the backward record is better than alternatives, does not endorse the probe scoring rule, and does not assume the separability stipulation survives its test. Those are real abstentions, not gaps I should fill with guesses.

The insufficiency I want to flag most clearly is this: the task asks what the requester should do, and the commitment field gives me a reformulation of the problem, one settled convergence, one specified move, one observation, and a list of abstentions. It does not give me the body's readings, the probe, the record, or the test. I can work on what follows from taking the commitments up, but I cannot reconstruct the body from them. Where I have written as if I know what the readings are, I have inferred from the commitment field's own labels, and those inferences are not load-bearing here.
commitments:
I am proposing that the commitment field is insufficient for the task as posed, not false. If someone produces the body and it turns out to contain the readings, probe, record, and test in a form that makes the commitment field's labels fully determinate, then my insufficiency claim weakens to a claim about what the selected view exposed rather than about the artifact. I do not have the body.

I am carrying the sequencing reformulation as a search instruction rather than as a thesis. The instruction is: look for a this-week action that is not one of the contested moves. If the search returns nothing, I would drop the reformulation rather than defend it. If the search returns something, that something still has to face the requester's actual flat, which I do not have.

I am carrying the quiet-week convergence as a chain-level claim whose evidential value depends on a contrast class the chain has not specified. I am not claiming quiet weeks are uninformative. I am claiming that without a contrast class, the convergence is weaker than the commitment field's phrasing suggests.

I am carrying the avoidant-friend approach as the best-specified move in the commitment field, with the attached cost that further avoidance counts against it. I am adding that one flat is a small case, so neither outcome is strong evidence. If tried, the result should be recorded as a single case, not as a confirmation or refutation.

I am adding a use for the load-position observation: identify the requester's position before choosing a proposal, and do it with care because stating it is itself one of the contested moves. I do not have evidence that this ordering helps, and it could backfire if the requester's self-assessment is disputed.

I am not committing to any ranking among the readings, to any order between a private record and the avoidant-friend conversation, to who the requester is in the flat, to the backward record being better or worse than alternatives, to the probe scoring rule being correct, or to the separability stipulation surviving its test. Those abstentions are real.

The unresolved problems I am leaving open: whether the requester's position constrains the available moves in the way the commitment field suggests; whether a probe run under a different scoring rule would count as the same probe or a divergent one; whether the quiet-week convergence has a contrast class; and whether the sequencing reformulation is a genuine addition or a restatement. I am holding all of this as fallible and as something I would revise on seeing the body.
